claims.statement: For every m : Nat, a ≤ b, and arbitrary E : (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ positive at every exponent vector in [a,b]^m, there exists a finite nonempty family with coordinate slopes in [a,b]^m and offsets o(h^a) as h → 0+, such that for any h_n → 0+, any unrestricted p_n → p ∈ [a,b]^m, and any label eventually weakly active against every family label at (h_n,p_n), every coordinate satisfies |p_i − slope_i| < E(slope).
assumptions: pointwise positivity of E on the full cube; no continuity or computability of E
claims.novelty_boundary: Formal verification of the arbitrary-positive-tolerance affine lemma attributed by the source manuscript to OpenAI release 149. No mathematical novelty, priority, or external acceptance is claimed. This lemma alone is not the complete endotactic permanence theorem.
claims.costs: Lean proof uses classical choice, compactness, finite families, and existing real-power asymptotics. The family construction is noncomputable as formalized; no useful bound on family size, cover size, thresholds, or numerical activity cutoff is established. E remains opaque except for pointwise positivity.
claims.falsifier: A Lean kernel failure under the pinned Lean 4.28/mathlib dependencies; an unexpected nonstandard axiom; a mismatch between the elaborated interface and the stated cube, sequence, tie, or tolerance quantifiers; or a concrete counterexample to the theorem interface.
claims.next_gate: Independently review the formalized affine lemma against the pinned source; then formalize the later weighted essential-source drift, Carathéodory plateau/continuation, and rational-rate clock steps before claiming full permanence. Complete a current primary-literature and priority audit.

claims.falsifier: A failure of the Lean 4.28 replay, an unexpected axiom, an implicit arbitrary Filter parameter in the public signature, or a mismatch in the uniform quantifiers over h, cube points, labels, ties, or coordinates.

claims.statement: For a nonempty finite family of differentiable real functions, if its pointwise minimum is differentiable at x, every active branch has the same derivative as that minimum; an active branch exists.
assumptions: Lean 4.28 elaboration and the matching cached mathlib build
all finite-family branches are differentiable at x
the finite pointwise minimum is differentiable at x
claims.novelty_boundary: Formal pointwise derivative identity used by the source finite-minimum chain rule. It is not an a.e. theorem for Caratheodory trajectories and is not the full permanence theorem.
claims.costs: The Lean proof applies Fermat theorem to each active branch minus the pointwise minimum. It does not prove absolute continuity of a finite minimum, almost-everywhere differentiability, or the trajectory differential inclusion.
claims.falsifier: A Lean replay failure, unexpected axiom, missing tie quantifier, or a mismatch in the pointwise finite-infimum interface.
claims.next_gate: Formalize the a.e. finite-minimum chain rule for absolutely continuous branch functions and connect the branches to a Caratheodory trajectory.

claims.statement: For any 0<h0≤hP<1, the capped square-root scale sequence starts at h0, follows h_(n+1)=min(sqrt(h_n),hP), and reaches hP at a finite index. If each scale-n plateau entry yields the next plateau within a supplied waiting bound W(n), then some time no later than the sum of the first N waiting bounds lies in the common hP plateau. Smaller-scale logarithmic boxes contain larger-scale boxes, so an old plateau inside the square-root box lies in the next-scale box.
assumptions: Lean 4.28 elaboration and matching cached mathlib build
positive initial and cap scales with h0≤hP<1
the one-step transition premise: from any time in the scale-n plateau, a later time in the next plateau exists within W(n)
claims.novelty_boundary: Formalizes the scale arithmetic, box order, and finite waiting-time composition in the source absorber argument. It is conditional on the one-scale dynamical entry rule and does not establish permanence.
claims.costs: Uses the exact exponential/logarithm closed form and 2^n→∞. No network trajectory, existence, invariance, or entry estimate is proved by this component.
claims.falsifier: A replay failure, unexpected axiom, incorrect recurrence/cap interface, or a scale-box containment error.
claims.next_gate: Derive the one-step transition premise from the measurable-rate vector field using weighted drift, the finite-minimum AC bridge, plateau invariance, and global continuation.
